facts.text: Mesa was originally called Bluff Wells, then Judson, before becoming Mesa, a stop on the Northern Pacific Railroad line between Ainsworth and Spokane.
In 1948 the Columbia Basin Irrigation Project brought water, transforming Mesa from a dry coulee into a thriving agricultural community.
The city sits in Esquatzel Coulee, a depression a few hundred feet below the surrounding hills, giving Mesa a unique lowland landscape.
The Historic Preservation Office is inviting residents to share stories about the Lehi and Washington‑Escobedo Heritage Neighborhoods, aiming to create digital story maps that bring history to life.
